_comment: Predicate registry. The vocabulary is CLOSED: 'vocabulary' is the complete set of predicates that may be stored, and a write whose predicate is still not in it after folding is refused where the caller can see it — kb_extract reports it in 'skipped' with the nearest candidates, kb_fact_add errors naming this file. 'single_valued' predicates auto-retire a prior object during kb_extract consolidation, but only when the subject matches 'single_valued_subjects' — cardinality is a property of (subject, predicate), not of the predicate. A ticket has one status; a repo accumulates them. Everything else keeps both objects. The subject pattern requires a separator or # before the trailing digits, so ticket and issue ids (tkt-4821, pr_#412, svc-api#59) match while names that merely end in a digit (web3, oauth2, sqlite3, es2022) do not. 'aliases' fold synonyms onto one canonical predicate so kb_fact_query, which matches on the predicate, does not under-return across synonym silos; every alias source is a spelling of its target, never a neighbouring meaning — 'implements' and 'fixes' both name a change closing work and stay separate, because one says what was built and the other what stopped hurting. Spelling variance that carries no meaning is folded without a list entry: hyphens and apostrophes, and a leading copula ('is_source_of_truth_for' -> 'source_of_truth_for'). Inflection folds too, but only onto a name this file already registers ('deploys_to' -> 'deployed_to'), so an unregistered pair like 'missing'/'missed' is never merged on morphology alone. Nothing single-valued is inflectable, for the same reason no inverse touches one: an inflection of a lifecycle noun is usually a verb meaning something else, and 'tkt-42 states that retries must be bounded' folded onto 'state' would retire the ticket's real lifecycle value to store a quotation. 'inverses' fold the mirrored spelling of a relationship onto one direction, swapping subject and object — the extractor picks a direction per call, and two live rows for one relationship retire independently. Each direction here is the one the graph already uses more, and none of them are single-valued, so the fold cannot change what retires what. 'work_item_object' predicates are asymmetric in roles rather than in spelling: the thing being built goes in the object, so a subject matching 'work_item_pattern' opposite an object that does not is a swapped pair, and folds. Only predicates whose subject must be a BUILDER belong here. A ticket cannot build code, so it cannot be the subject of 'implements' — but it can perfectly well target a problem, so 'addresses', 'fixes', 'closes' and 'resolves' take a work item on either side and are not listed. 'work_item_pattern' is an unanchored token: a subject must equal it, an object need only begin with it, since a work item under a label (tkt-19_step_1) still makes the row a relationship between two work items. It excludes a leading pull-request marker because a PR is an implementer, not a work item, and takes a single word before the separator so a compound id ending in a PR number (tkt-19-repo-pr-277) is not read as one. Extend or override per install with <KB_DIR>/predicates.json using the same shape — 'many_valued' there removes a built-in, 'vocabulary' and the older key 'preferred' both add storable predicates, 'aliases' and 'inverses' merge with these, 'work_item_object' adds to that list, and either pattern there replaces the one here.
_vocabulary_comment: Why these and not others. An open vocabulary produced a log rather than a graph: 13,090 distinct predicates over 31k facts, 10,004 of them written exactly once, and one family — 'this merged / shipped / was fixed / deployed' — spelled more than 400 ways. Under that, a predicate query returns a fraction of its matching rows and single-valued retirement stops firing the moment the next fact arrives under a different spelling. Both failures are invisible, because every row still reads as a well-formed fact on its own. Two rules decided membership. (1) Volume: a predicate the store already uses at scale is legitimate whatever we would have chosen from a blank page — 'is' and 'has' are junk-drawer relations and both are kept, because refusing a top-ten predicate routes thousands of true assertions into 'skipped' and teaches callers to reach for a wrong-but-accepted predicate instead, which corrupts the graph in a way a coarse edge does not. Splitting them is a later job with a migration behind it, not something to do by rejection. (2) Role: a slot an engineering graph needs even where the census spread it thin — 'runs_on', 'stored_in', 'talks_to', 'proposes', 'reverts', 'drops'. What earned no slot: anything whose only reader is a test, and anything compound. A compound name ('merge_to_main_deploys_to', 'tracks_revert_of', 'migration_proposed_in') is a sentence wearing a predicate's clothes, and it is what the singleton tail is made of — those decompose onto a listed predicate or they are skipped. The list is deliberately well short of a round hundred. Padding it with plausible entries nobody has written would re-open the hole it exists to close, and an unlisted predicate is not lost: it comes back with its nearest listed candidates attached, which is the signal that says whether the vocabulary or the assertion was the thing that was wrong. Note one interaction: the copula strip reduces 'is_a' to 'a' before the alias map is consulted, so the alias is written in its natural form below and resolves through that key.
